statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, call a list S a valid divisible subset of nums if (i) every element of S occurs in nums, (ii) all elements of S are pairwise distinct, and (iii) for all distinct indices a,b of S, S[a] % S[b] = 0 or S[b] % S[a] = 0. Then r itself is a valid divisible subset of nums, and for every valid divisible subset S of nums, len(S) <= len(r).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2_000_000_000; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, if i != j then nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2_000_000_000; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, if i != j then nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that r[i] = nums[j].
